A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching authors, central models and principal theorems despite the shortened title. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations and v2's figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original qualitative experimental outcomes. Section 3.4 describes structures recovered in the authors' CE-DUFM experiments and states that Assumption 1 held in every observed DNC case, although no experimental figures or detailed protocols are supplied.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original deep-UFM simulations and MNIST/CIFAR-10 network experiments, including losses, convergence frequencies, ranks, singular values and logit matrices.

M1.justification: The analyzed model family changes substantially: v1's minimally nonlinear MSE model, including Hadamard-power activation variants in Appendices A/C, is removed. V2 instead develops the unequal-class-size CE formulation. The principal linear/ReLU CE architecture and regularized objective remain unchanged; this is a change in model scope rather than a redesigned optimization algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual image-classification experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 to the deep-UFM numerical observations reported in v1. The new class-imbalance material is theoretical and does not establish additional empirical population coverage.

E2.justification: The comparison remains between DNC and lower-rank solutions, using the same constructed solution families and DNC loss bounds. V2 quantifies these comparisons and extends them to full networks, but adds no distinct competing learning method.

E3.justification: The newly reported full-network experiments introduce ResNet-20 backbones, specified linear/ReLU heads, UFM-style versus all-parameter regularization, loss and spectral diagnostics, balanced MNIST subsampling and batch-size-10,000 training. These are protocols for added experiments; newly supplied UFM hyperparameters do not establish that v1's unspecified experiments were changed or rerun.

E4.justification: Figures 2 and 5 add quantitative sensitivity analyses of DNC frequency and converged rank versus width and regularization, beyond v1's qualitative observations. The full-network experiments also examine whether low-rank behavior persists with ReLU activations and standard weight decay, providing substantial additional evidence about applicability.

E5.justification: V2 reports averages over 10 runs for Figures 2 and 5 and explicitly identifies most other experiments as single indicative runs. V1 provides no corresponding run counts. This adds reporting transparency without establishing an increase in runs; confidence intervals, error bars and seed specifications remain absent.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive concrete outcomes: loss trajectories, DNC probabilities, average ranks, logit heatmaps and singular-value spectra. Section 4 reports four singular values above 10^-6 for MNIST and three for CIFAR-10 in the linear-head experiments. These are newly reported results, not demonstrated same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Theorem 4 strengthens leading-order Hessian positivity to positivity of the full Hessian, with a new proof. V2 adds Theorem 6 on asymptotic Hessian-norm ratios and a rank-two diagonally superior construction, improving v1's class-dependent bound. Appendices A/C replace the MSE/Hadamard-power results with imbalance theorems and proofs. Definitions and proofs explicitly handle general n, and DNC3 broadens collinearity to linear combinations. V1's ReLU Theorem 6 survives as Theorem 7 with unchanged class/depth thresholds.

C1.justification: The central claims about DNC suboptimality, low-rank bias and width-dependent persistence remain. The contribution statement strengthens one retained claim from a positive-semidefinite leading-order Hessian to a positive-semidefinite full Hessian at sufficiently small regularization. The new experiments primarily support the existing scientific thesis.

C2.justification: V2 adds the interpretation that asymptotically comparable Hessian flatness cannot alone explain preferential convergence to DNC, and emphasizes initialization and implicit bias as unresolved mechanisms. It removes v1's extended criticism of the single-layer UFM regularization assumption and adds explicit limitations concerning generalization, robustness and underparameterized regimes. The imbalance discussion also identifies STEP imbalance and unspecified depth bounds as applicability limits.

D1.justification: V2 supplies substantial previously absent experimental documentation: ResNet-20 architecture, head depths and widths, learning rates and regularization coefficients in figure captions, plus sampling, input standardization and batch size in Appendix D. These disclosures make the numerical evidence substantially more reproducible, although code access, hardware and initialization specifics remain unreported.

R1.justification: V2 removes the entire loss-surface related-work strand covering spin-glass models, Hessian spectra and shallow/linear-network landscapes. It adds work on imbalance, next-token prediction, multivariate regression and initialization/implicit bias. Appendix A newly develops the relationship to Thrampoulidis et al. and Hong and Ling, substantially reshaping the literature coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, conclusion and proof exposition are extensively rewritten and condensed. Contributions become a bullet list, terminology shifts from DUFM to deep UFM, and the background is consolidated. A numerical-experiments section and Appendix D are added, while Appendices A/C are repurposed.

P2.justification: V1 has no figures or tables. V2 introduces eight multi-panel figures across the main text and Appendix D, displaying loss curves, parameter sweeps, logit heatmaps and singular-value spectra. This substantially changes the visual presentation of evidence, while retaining the single-column document format.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for the central thesis: the full-Hessian analysis addresses the limitation of v1's leading-order argument, the rank-two construction sharpens the theory, and specified simulations and real-network experiments replace largely undocumented empirical assertions. Removing the MSE/Hadamard-power appendix reduces theoretical breadth, and convergence explanations remain heuristic with mostly single-run network evidence. Nevertheless, the gains in theoretical support, empirical substantiation and reproducibility constitute a substantial overall improvement.
